title: Cluster Evaluation Quiz
description: Test your understanding of cluster evaluation

questions.question: What is the main difference between internal and external clustering evaluation metrics?
options: Internal metrics are always more accurate than external metrics
Internal metrics use only the data and cluster assignments, while external metrics compare against ground truth labels
External metrics are faster to compute than internal metrics
Internal metrics work only with K-Means, while external metrics work with any algorithm
questions.explanation: Internal metrics evaluate clustering quality using only the data and cluster assignments without external information, while external metrics compare clustering results against known ground truth labels.

questions.question: What does a silhouette score of 0.8 indicate?
options: Strong clustering structure with well-separated clusters
questions.explanation: A silhouette score of 0.8 indicates strong clustering structure. Scores between 0.7-1.0 represent strong structure, meaning points are well-matched to their clusters and well-separated from other clusters.

questions.question: For the Davies-Bouldin Index, what does a lower value indicate?
questions.explanation: For the Davies-Bouldin Index, lower values indicate better clustering quality. This metric measures the average similarity between each cluster and its most similar cluster, so lower values mean better separation.

questions.question: What is the range of the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI)?
questions.explanation: The Adjusted Rand Index ranges from -1 to +1, where +1 indicates perfect agreement with ground truth, 0 indicates random clustering, and negative values indicate worse than random performance.

questions.question: Which metric would be most appropriate for comparing clusterings with different numbers of clusters when you don't have ground truth labels?
questions.explanation: The Calinski-Harabasz Index is an internal metric that's particularly good for comparing clusterings with different numbers of clusters. It measures the ratio of between-cluster to within-cluster variance and doesn't require ground truth labels.

questions.question: What does the V-Measure combine to evaluate clustering quality?
questions.explanation: V-Measure is the harmonic mean of homogeneity (each cluster contains only members of a single class) and completeness (all members of a class are assigned to the same cluster).

questions.question: Why is it recommended to use multiple evaluation metrics rather than relying on a single metric?
options: To make the evaluation process more complex
Because different metrics capture different aspects of clustering quality
Because single metrics are always wrong
questions.explanation: Different metrics capture different aspects of clustering quality (separation, compactness, agreement with ground truth, etc.). Using multiple metrics provides a more comprehensive and reliable evaluation than any single metric alone.

questions.question: Which of the following is a limitation of the silhouette score?
options: It only works with K-Means clustering
It is computationally expensive with O(n²) complexity
questions.explanation: The silhouette score has O(n²) computational complexity because it requires calculating distances between all pairs of points, making it expensive for large datasets. It can also be biased toward convex clusters.
